newsitem.title: UK: DOW DUTCH PETCHEM CRACKER BACK UP A WEEK EARLY.
newsitem.headline: DOW DUTCH PETCHEM CRACKER BACK UP A WEEK EARLY.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co said on Monday its 500,000 tonnes a year petrochemical cracker in Terneuzen, the Netherlands, was operating at full rates after it came back onstream on Saturday.
A company source said the restart had been around a week earlier than expected, because Dow had been able to replace a damaged compressor with a unit it held in its stores.
"We didn't try to repair the damage (which would have taken a couple of weeks)," the source said, pointing out that locating a replacement would normally have taken at least a month.
The Terneuzen cracker came down with compressor damage on July 27 with Dow predicting a mid-August restart given the expected repair lead-time.

Since July 27, Repsol's 550,000 tonnes a year Tarragona, Spain cracker has been confirmed down once - for a few days - and was rumoured down again for five to six days last week, but also restarted over the weekend, traders said.
